review_summary: D1's central claim is FACTUALLY CORRECT this time — RED_CONFIRMED is verifiably the TDD guard's bypass state (tdd-guard.test.ts:345 'returns null when state is RED_CONFIRMED (allowed)'; mcp-tools.ts:107 'Use state RED_CONFIRMED to bypass the TDD guard'), and server.ts:220 is verifiably the active-session early return. However the plan has a hard blocker in Workstream D: the bulkTddTransition call chain passes through TWO files that appear in NO task's Files list (targets/opencode/plugins/sentinal-helpers.ts and src/sidecar/client-routes.ts), and fixing that creates a same-wave Task 7/Task 8 overlap on client-routes.ts, directly contradicting the plan's 'no same-wave overlaps' plan_impact claim. Workstream B does not satisfy the user's literal ask ('restart itself') and has a placement under-specification plus a chicken-and-egg that makes it inert for the first upgrade.

issues.title: The bulkTddTransition call chain has two files in NO task — Task 7 will break the OpenCode plugin
issues.description:
The plan states (line 70, 130, 587) that the plugin's call sites are `sentinal.ts:306,316`. Verified: those lines do NOT call `bulkTddTransition` or `sidecar.tddTransition`. The real chain is:

`sentinal.ts:306/316` -> `transitionTddState()` at **`targets/opencode/plugins/sentinal-helpers.ts:259-269`** -> `sidecar.tddTransition(action, specId)` at **`src/sidecar/client-routes.ts:129-133`** -> POST `/tdd-state/transition` -> `handleTddTransitionRequest` (`tdd-routes.ts:60-82`) -> `bulkTddTransition` (`tdd-routes.ts:26`).

Grep confirms `bulkTddTransition` has exactly ONE production caller: `tdd-routes.ts:76`. There are no CLI callers and no Claude Code caller (`src/hooks/tdd-tracker.ts` does its own per-cycle updates at :95-128, not the bulk route), so the plan is right that the plugin is the only consumer — but it named the wrong files.

Neither `targets/opencode/plugins/sentinal-helpers.ts` (nor its test `sentinal-helpers.test.ts`, which asserts the `tddTransition` signature at :33-56) nor `src/sidecar/client-routes.ts` appears in Task 7's or Task 12's Files list. Task 7 makes the project param required and 400s without it; the wire contract therefore cannot be honoured, and the plugin's TDD bulk transitions break.

Separately: `sidecarTddTrack` (the function containing :292-317) has no project value in scope at all — `setTddState` at :292-296 passes none. Task 12 edit 2 says 'record the project' without noting that a project must first be plumbed into `sidecarTddTrack`'s signature from its caller.
issues.suggested_fix: Add `src/sidecar/client-routes.ts` (extend `tddTransition(action, specId, projectPath)`) to Task 7's Files, and add `targets/opencode/plugins/sentinal-helpers.ts` + `sentinal-helpers.test.ts` (extend `transitionTddState` and `TddTransitionSidecar`) to Task 12's Files. Add an explicit sub-step to Task 12 edit 2: plumb a `projectPath` parameter into `sidecarTddTrack`'s signature from its call site, and pass it to BOTH `setTddState` (:292) and the two `transitionTddState` calls. Restate the plan's 'plugin call sites' references from `sentinal.ts:306,316` to the full four-hop chain so the implementer cannot stop at the wrong file.

issues.title: Task 7 and Task 8 both need src/sidecar/client-routes.ts in Wave 3 — a same-wave overlap the plan claims does not exist
issues.description:
Line 152 asserts 'no same-wave overlaps across all 4 waves', and line 148 says Wave 3's Tasks 7-10 'touch four disjoint areas'. Task 8 explicitly owns `src/sidecar/client-routes.ts` (adds `requestRetire()` alongside `insertNotification` at :339). Per the previous issue, Task 7 must ALSO edit `src/sidecar/client-routes.ts` to add the project argument to `tddTransition` (:129-133). Both are Wave 3.

Per `.sentinal/skills/sentinal-parity-baselines` and the wave rule cited in the plan's own Wave 4 note, a same-wave overlap on OpenCode shares one working directory and corrupts work. This is precisely the failure the `plan_impact` run was supposed to catch — it did not, because Task 7's Files list omitted the file.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-run `plan_impact` after correcting Task 7's and Task 12's Files lists. Then resolve the overlap one of two ways: (a) move Task 8 to Wave 4 so Task 7 owns `client-routes.ts` alone in Wave 3, or (b) merge the `client-routes.ts` edits into a single owner task. Update the line-152 plan_impact paragraph with the new result rather than leaving the stale 'no same-wave overlaps' claim.

issues.title: Task 7's 400-on-missing-project is silently swallowed by the plugin, so the fail-closed design is invisible
issues.description:
Task 7 decides (line 426) 'A missing project must be a 400, not an unscoped sweep.' The design is right, but the only caller swallows it: `transitionTddState` (`sentinal-helpers.ts:259-269`) wraps the call in `try { await sidecar.tddTransition(...) } catch { /* non-fatal */ }`, and its own caller `sidecarTddTrack` has a second swallowing `catch` at `sentinal.ts:318-320`. `client-routes.ts`'s `post` failure will therefore produce no log, no notification, and no user-visible signal.

If Task 12 misses any of the plumbing (see issue 1), TDD confirm_red/confirm_green stops working entirely and NOTHING reports it — the exact 'signal reaches nobody' shape this plan exists to fix, reintroduced by the plan itself. Task 7's DoD 'A request with no project is rejected, not treated as "all"' is satisfiable by a unit test on the route while production stays silently broken.
issues.suggested_fix: Add to Task 7's DoD: the 400 path must `logSidecar` a distinct message naming the missing project. Add to Task 12's DoD: `transitionTddState`'s catch must log to the plugin debug log (`~/.sentinal/plugin.debug.log`) rather than swallow, OR the helper must fail fast in a way `sentinal.test.ts` asserts. Add an integration-level DoD to Task 12 that drives the real helper against a real route and asserts `count` is returned (not that the call merely did not throw).

issues.title: Workstream B stops the sidecar but nothing restarts it — the user asked for 'restart itself'
issues.description:
The user request is that the sidecar 'recognise it is running a stale version and restart itself after some time'. Verified: `doShutdown` (`server.ts:169-195`) ends in `stopSidecar(...)` + `process.exit(0)`. There is no respawn. Task 5's DoD says only 'Retire shuts down once sessions are absent, with a distinct reason string'.

Per `.sentinal/rules/sentinal-sidecar.md`, `SidecarClient.connect()` returns `null` when the sidecar is down and 'hooks must handle this without erroring' — i.e. hooks degrade silently. Only `connectWithRetry()` (MCP startup path) calls `autoStartSidecar()`. So after a retire, a hook-only workload gets degraded behaviour with no sidecar until an MCP server happens to start. The plan never names who brings the new sidecar up, and 'retire' is never reconciled against the user's word 'restart'.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) add an explicit respawn step to the retire path in Task 5 (spawn the NEW binary detached before `process.exit(0)`, reusing `autoStartSidecar`'s spawn shape — and state how a spawn loop is prevented if the new binary is also stale), or (b) state explicitly in Key Decisions that retire is stop-only and cite the concrete evidence that the next consumer reliably autostarts, with a DoD test proving a hook-initiated `SidecarClient.connect()` after retire results in a running sidecar. Do not leave this implicit — it is the literal wording of the user's request.

issues.title: Task 5's 'after line 220' constraint is necessary but far from sufficient; two placements make retire never fire
issues.description:
Verified: `server.ts:220` is the `return` inside the `else` branch of 'active sessions with recent activity'. The plan's constraint is correct as far as it goes, but everything after :220 is a three-way fork and the plan picks none of them:

- Placed at :226 (immediately after the early return): retire bypasses the grace period, contradicting D2 ('reuses the existing grace period').
- Placed inside the `if (sessionsEverSeen)` branch (:227-235): correct for normal use, but a sidecar that never saw a session never retires.
- Placed in the `else` branch (:236-242): the gate is `Date.now() - lastActivityTime >= fallbackIdleMs` (30 min). `touchActivity()` is documented at :113-116 as 'Called on every incoming request'. A skew-detecting client that keeps POSTing `/retire` (Task 8, fired from `noteVersionSkew` on `tryConnect`, i.e. the hot path of every hook) RESETS `lastActivityTime` on every call — so the more aggressively the client asks for retirement, the longer retirement is deferred. That is a self-defeating loop the plan does not mention.

Task 5's DoD only tests the 'stays alive when active sessions exist' direction (mirroring `server.test.ts:705-733`). Nothing tests the never-saw-a-session case or the activity-reset interaction.
issues.suggested_fix: Name the exact insertion point in Task 5 (recommend: immediately before the `if (sessionsEverSeen)` at :227, with the retire branch applying its OWN grace accounting so D2 still holds, i.e. reuse `noSessionSince` rather than short-circuiting it). Add two DoD items: (1) a sidecar with `sessionsEverSeen === false` still retires within the grace period once stale; (2) repeated `/retire` POSTs (which call `touchActivity`) do not indefinitely defer shutdown — assert retirement occurs while requests are still arriving.

issues.title: Task 11 will surface OTHER projects' notifications and will zero the dashboard's unread badge globally
issues.description:
Verified: the `notifications` table (`migrations.ts:262-277`) has `spec_id TEXT REFERENCES specs(id)` and no project column — the plan's implicit premise. Consequences the plan does not address:

1. `getNotifications({unread: true, limit})` (`store-sessions.ts:213`) cannot be project-filtered. A SessionStart hook in project A will surface skew/vector/self-heal notifications produced while working in projects B and C. Task 11's DoD ('Unread notifications appear in SessionStart output') is satisfied by that wrong behaviour.
2. `markAllNotificationsRead()` (`store-sessions.ts:239`) takes NO arguments — it is global. If Task 11 uses it (line 553 offers it as an option), a session start in project A marks project B's unseen notifications read.
3. The dashboard is not made permanently empty (`api.ts:35` and `dashboard/server.ts:188` call `getNotifications({limit: 10})` unfiltered, so read items still render), but `getUnreadNotificationCount()` is consumed at `dashboard/server.ts:138` and `:201` and at `api.ts:115`, and the unread-filtered view at `api.ts:114` WILL go empty. The badge a human relies on becomes permanently 0 because a hook consumed it first.

Note the `specs.id` collision documented in `.sentinal/rules/sentinal-project.md` limitation 2 means even `spec_id` is not a safe project proxy.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a `project_path` column to `notifications` in the SAME migration as V13 (Task 2 already owns `migrations.ts`, and both writers are reachable), populate it in `insertNotification` (`store-sessions.ts:181-204`), and give `getNotifications` an optional project filter. Then Task 11 filters by `resolveProjectIdentity(input.cwd)`. Forbid `markAllNotificationsRead()` in Task 11 — use per-id `markNotificationRead` for exactly the ids surfaced. Add a DoD: 'a notification created for project B does not appear in, and is not marked read by, a SessionStart in project A' and 'the dashboard unread count is unaffected by notifications this hook did not surface'. If the column is deemed out of scope, Task 11 must be descoped to skew notifications only (matched by title/type), not all unread notifications.

issues.title: Workstream B is inert for the upgrade that installs it — the running sidecar is the OLD binary with no poll and no /retire route
issues.description:
The sidecar that needs to retire is by definition running pre-change code. It contains neither the `detectBinaryStaleness` interval (Task 3/5) nor the `/retire` route (Task 5). So on the first upgrade after this ships: the self-check cannot run, and the client's `requestRetire()` POST hits a sidecar whose `handleSidecarRequest` (documented at line 361 as 'the only handler that returns 404') returns 404. Workstream B only produces value from upgrade N+1 onward.

This is unavoidable, but it is not stated anywhere, and Goal Verification truth 7 ('`sentinal sidecar logs` contains a retire line after a simulated binary-mtime change') is only verifiable against a post-change sidecar — an implementer testing it against the live machine's currently-running sidecar will see nothing and may conclude the feature is broken.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a Key Decision stating the one-upgrade lag explicitly, and amend truth 7 to specify the sidecar must be restarted onto the new binary before the check is meaningful. Confirm in Task 8's DoD that a 404 from `/retire` is absorbed by the `.catch(() => {})` and produces no log spam on every hook invocation against an old sidecar.

issues.title: D1's 'permanently stranded' rationale is overstated — verify and rewrite, though the DELETE conclusion still stands
issues.description:
The load-bearing half of D1 is CORRECT and verified: RED_CONFIRMED is the TDD guard's bypass state (`src/hooks/tdd-guard.test.ts:345` 'returns null when state is RED_CONFIRMED (allowed)'; `src/tdd/mcp-tools.ts:107` 'Use state RED_CONFIRMED to bypass the TDD guard and allow editing an implementation file'). A surviving NULL-project RED row would indeed be a bypass, not a block, so the rationale does not invert.

But 'nothing could ever transition or delete them' is false. Only `bulkTddTransition` gains the project filter. `setTddState` upserts on `file_path` (UNIQUE per V7, `migrations.ts:285-299`) and would repopulate `project_path` on the next write to that file; `tdd_clear` / per-file clearing (`tdd-tracker.ts:128`) has no project clause. NULL rows are reachable by every path except the bulk one. An adversarial reader who checks this will distrust the whole decision.

Also unmentioned: DELETE is the fail-CLOSED direction (removing a bypass re-arms the guard), which strengthens D1 — but it means a user mid-RED-cycle across an upgrade is suddenly blocked from editing their impl file with no explanation.
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite D1 to: (1) cite `tdd-guard.test.ts:345` as the evidence that RED_CONFIRMED is a bypass; (2) replace 'permanently stranded' with the accurate claim — NULL rows are invisible to the project-scoped bulk transition specifically, so a RED bypass survives until that exact file is written again, which is indefinite in practice; (3) state that DELETE is the fail-closed direction and is therefore the safe default. Add to Task 2's DoD: when the deleted count is non-zero, emit a notification (Task 11 now makes those visible) explaining that in-flight TDD cycles were reset by the upgrade.

issues.title: The three Workstream B mechanisms are not actually unified — the client-triggered path never notifies
issues.description:
The user explicitly asked for a COMBINATION of notify + client-triggered retire + sidecar self-check. Task 5 line 360 wires `notifySkewOnce` only into the self-detection branch ('Wire `detectBinaryStaleness` into the same interval ... and call `notifySkewOnce` when it flips'). The `/retire` route handler (`retire-routes.ts`, Task 5) is described only as 'sets the flag and returns ok' — no notification. So a client-detected skew retires silently, and the notify channel fires only if the sidecar independently notices. On a sidecar whose `detectBinaryStaleness` mtime snapshot was taken at boot but whose `--version` confirm fails (Task 3 returns 'not stale' conservatively on any failure), the client path is the ONLY detector and it is the one that does not notify.

Second ambiguity: `notifySkewOnce` is 'version-scoped', but which version keys the settings entry? `getSentinalVersion()` returns three different values by context (plan line 95), and the client-triggered path knows the client's version while the sidecar knows its own. If the two paths key differently, the once-per-version guard is once-per-version-per-path and can fire twice; if one path uses the 'dev' fallback, it fires once for all future versions.
issues.suggested_fix: Have `handleRetireRequest` call `notifySkewOnce` too, so both detectors converge on notify AND flag rather than just the flag. Specify in Task 4 the exact settings key format and which version supplies it (recommend the sidecar's own `getSentinalVersion()` plus the observed new version, e.g. `skew:<own>-><new>`, so the guard is per-transition not per-process). Add a DoD to Task 5: 'a client-triggered retire emits the notification and log line exactly once, and a subsequent self-detection of the same skew emits none.'

issues.title: Task 10's prose-drift mitigation is scoped to the tool description only — shipped rules and embedded assets also document the old behaviour
issues.description:
Task 10 correctly cites `.sentinal/skills/sentinal-schema-prose-drift`, but its Files list contains only `src/opencode/native-tdd-status.ts` and `src/tdd/mcp-tools.ts`. The skill's whole point is that shipped prose drifts independently of source. Grep shows the old 'lists all active TDD states' semantics and `tdd_status` usage recipes are also carried in `src/cli/embedded-assets.ts` (e.g. :18933, :20292, :26796, :28213 — generated copies of shipped rules and `/sync` recipes), and `.sentinal/rules/sentinal-mcp-servers.md` documents `tdd_status` as 'Read TDD cycle state (per file or all active)'. None are in any task.

Additionally, if the fix touches anything under `targets/*/rules/`, `.sentinal/skills/sentinal-parity-baselines` requires regenerating parity baselines — and warns that regeneration rewrites the ENTIRE fixture directory, which is hazardous for a Wave-3 task running in parallel.
issues.suggested_fix: Extend Task 10's Files to include the shipped rule text that documents `tdd_status`/`tdd_set_state` scope in both `targets/claude-code/rules/` and `targets/opencode/rules/` (keeping them in sync per `.sentinal/rules/sentinal-dual-target.md`), plus `.sentinal/rules/sentinal-mcp-servers.md`. If `targets/*/rules/` is touched, move Task 10 to be the sole Wave owner of that directory and add the baseline-regeneration step and `target-parity.test.ts` to its Verify.

issues.title: No task regenerates src/cli/embedded-assets.ts, so the installer may ship the old plugin — and two Goal Verification greps are unreliable because of it
issues.description:
`src/cli/embedded-assets.ts` contains a generated copy of the OpenCode plugin bundle — line 16309 is the current compaction code (`const hasRedState = tddStates.some((cycle) => cycle.state === "RED_CONFIRMED")`) and :15942 is the current `tddTransition`. Task 12's Verify runs `bun run build:opencode` and `src/cli/target-assets.test.ts`, but nothing runs `scripts/embed-assets.mjs`. If embedding is not part of the release build, the CLI installer ships pre-change plugin code while every test passes.

This also undermines Goal Verification: truth 2 ('grep `startsWith(projectPath)` returns nothing outside tests') and truth 8 ('grep `getNotifications` appears outside `src/dashboard/`') are plain greps that will hit `embedded-assets.ts` and `targets/opencode/dist/sentinal.mjs` regardless of source correctness — truth 2 produces a false FAIL if assets are stale and a false PASS is possible for truth 8.
issues.suggested_fix: Confirm whether `scripts/embed-assets.mjs` runs as part of `release-build.mjs`; if it does not run automatically, add it to Task 12's Verify. Reword truths 2 and 8 to exclude generated paths explicitly (`--glob '!src/cli/embedded-assets.ts' --glob '!targets/*/dist/**'`) so they measure source, not build output.

issues.title: Task 6's back-compat DoD reopens the exact fail-open class Task 7 closes
issues.description: Task 7 argues (line 426) that an optional project param 'reproduces the bug the moment a caller forgets it' and must therefore be REQUIRED and fail closed. Task 6's DoD then states the opposite for the store layer: '`listActiveTddStates` with no project still returns everything (back-compat)'. Task 10 then has to remember to always pass one. That is the same forget-and-silently-sweep shape, one layer down, and it is what allowed the original defect. It is defensible for a read path (fail-open is the safe direction for reads, and the plan says so for relative paths at line 91) but the plan never reconciles the two policies, so an implementer reading Task 6 and Task 7 back to back gets contradictory guidance.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to Key Decisions stating the policy explicitly: WRITE and DESTRUCTIVE paths fail closed on a missing project; READ paths fail open and default to unscoped, with the scoping applied at the caller. Cross-reference it from Task 6 and Task 7 so the asymmetry reads as deliberate.

issues.title: /retire is an unauthenticated shutdown trigger on a shared local endpoint
issues.description: The sidecar listens on `~/.sentinal/sidecar.sock` and a localhost HTTP port fallback (`.sentinal/rules/sentinal-sidecar.md`). Adding `/retire` gives any local process a one-request way to schedule the shared sidecar's shutdown, affecting every project and every concurrently-running Claude Code / OpenCode session on the machine. Existing routes are equally unauthenticated so this is not a new class, but `/retire` is the first route whose sole purpose is to terminate the process, and D3 makes it deliberately idempotent and unverified.
issues.suggested_fix: Have `/retire` require the caller's observed version in the body and have the sidecar verify the skew itself (via `detectBinaryStaleness`) before honouring it, so the route is a hint rather than a command. This also closes the gap where a client with a wrong version notion can retire a perfectly current sidecar.
